claims.statement: For every eligible ordinary tree T and p, if the exact selected sum S(T,p) is positive, then some original favorable leaf tag v and independent (p-1)-set A of H_v meeting W_v have at least p vertices addable in H_v. Consequently, if every such marked set for every selected tag has at most p-1 addable vertices, then S(T,p)<=0.
claims.scope: Retained as a conditional necessary criterion and sufficient obstruction to positivity under the exact contract eligibility, selector, original support and neighborhood definitions, and tag multiplicities. It does not resolve the primary aggregate target.
claims.reason: retained: the bipartite addable-vertex capacity and exact marked-extension incidence count give (p-1)S=(2a+1-3p)Q-E with nonnegative per-set deficits and multiply marked extensions counted once in C. Since eligibility makes p-1 and 2a+1-3p positive, S>0 forces a selected deficit below 2a+1-3p, equivalent to e_v(A)>=p. Conversely, the asserted uniform bound makes D>=cQ and forces S<=0. The source proof checks alpha(H_v)=a-1 and uses the unchanged selector; no material proof gap was found. This remains conditional and supplies no primary verdict.

limitations: The conditional criterion does not prove the addability bound for all eligible ordinary trees and does not establish the primary aggregate inequality.
No positive witness or primary counterexample is supplied; the listed negative-sum controls do not exercise the positive-sum antecedent.
